episodes.title: OpenAI: When AI Agents Use Computers Faster Than You
episodes.about: AI agents are approaching a point where they can use computers faster than expert humans, turning the user interface itself into a universal way for AI to interact with software. OpenAI's Ari Weinstein and James Sun argue that computer use is now entering its scaling moment, and explain how computer-using agents are already navigating legacy ERPs, reconciling financial data, handling procurement, and operating software without APIs or custom integrations. They also discuss why the harness around the model can matter as much as model intelligence, and how enterprises can set deterministic guardrails around agent behavior.
episodes.why: Out today: OpenAI's Ari Weinstein and James Sun say computer use is entering its scaling moment - agents already navigating legacy ERPs and reconciling financial data with no APIs.

episodes.title: Kevin Roose is AGI-pilled. Why aren't you?
episodes.about: Kevin Roose, longtime New York Times reporter and former Hard Fork host, just left The Times with Casey Newton to launch the new tech podcast Machine Gods. He joins Nilay Patel to talk about launching Machine Gods, what it is like to go from mainstream media to independent creator, and his new book The AGI Chronicles, a reported dive into the companies racing to build machine intelligence - and why he has become convinced AGI is coming.
episodes.why: Out today: Kevin Roose, a week after launching Machine Gods, makes his AGI case to Nilay Patel and talks through the reporting behind The AGI Chronicles.

episodes.title: How I'm Actually Using AI Right Now (Including Claude Duet)
episodes.about: Claude Duet's launch is an opportunity to take stock of how NLW is actually using AI today. From strategy and research to coding, content creation and data analysis, he breaks down his current AI stack and which models work best for which tasks. Then, a comparison of ChatGPT Dots and Claude Duet, and why proactive personal agents might finally be finding their place in his workflow.
episodes.why: Claude Duet just launched; NLW uses it to audit his real AI stack task by task, then compares Duet with ChatGPT Dots on proactive personal agents.

episodes.title: When ChatGPT writes your obituary
episodes.about: Donna Guthrie had obituaries on her mind after her brother passed away in May. She recently celebrated her 80th birthday and started wondering how she might be remembered, so she asked ChatGPT to write her obituary. It is the topic of today's 'Uncanny AI,' Marketplace Tech's regular segment about unsettling experiences with this tech, with technologist and artist Michelle Huang weighing in on whether this is creepy or healthy.
episodes.why: Eight minutes: an 80-year-old asked ChatGPT to write her obituary, and Marketplace's Uncanny AI segment asks whether that is creepy or healthy.

episodes.title: How bots are overtaking humans on the internet
episodes.about: There are now more bots than humans online. What does that mean for how we experience the internet? The Indicator looks at what changes when most web traffic is no longer human, and whether bots and humans can peacefully coexist online.
episodes.why: Discovery pick - The Indicator is Planet Money's short daily economics show, new here: bots now outnumber humans online, and it asks what that does to the internet people actually use.
